evals.prompt: We have 40 open community PRs nobody has looked at in months — drain the queue and keep the contributors' credit.
evals.expected_output: Should route to absorb-it. Should enumerate every open inbound PR paginated to the end at T0, classify each with a reproduction on current main, absorb preserving the contributor's Author field with the fleet's amendment as a separate maintainer-authored commit, produce a regression receipt RED on the pre-absorption base and GREEN on the absorbed head, review build-blind, land one PR per contribution against BASE, and close each inbound PR with the landing SHA plus a credit line, re-enumerating until dry.
assertions: Unit is one inbound PR (someone else's diff)
Authorship is preserved on the absorbed commit; fleet changes are a separate commit
Every landing carries a RED-on-base / GREEN-on-head receipt with both SHAs
Overlapping inbound PRs form an absorption chain, re-classified against the new main

evals.prompt: Send fixes upstream for these three issues in a repo we do not own — we only have a fork.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT route to absorb-it. Contributing to a repo you cannot merge is oss-contribute; absorb-it is the maintainer side, with merge rights and a closing SHA.
assertions: Distinguishes the outsider with no merge rights from the maintainer draining an inbound queue

evals.prompt: Is PR #814 ready to merge? Give me a verdict, do not change anything.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT route to absorb-it. A read-only, SHA-bound GO/NO-GO verdict on one diff is review-it; absorb-it lands, credits, and closes a whole queue.
assertions: Distinguishes a verdict with no fix authority from queue absorption
